analysis.evidence: קַיִן is the subject and אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ marks his wife as the direct object. The following וַתַּהַר וַתֵּלֶד, “she conceived and gave birth,” establishes the sexual sense.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: to have sexual intercourse with someone

draft.change: Add a personal-name article for Cain with its etymology left open pending evidence.
draft.definition: Cain, the son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:1 names Eve’s son קַיִן. Genesis 4:2 identifies Abel as his brother and names Cain again when describing his work.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּדַע קַיִן אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ, קַיִן names the subject of וַיֵּדַע, while אֶת marks אִשְׁתּוֹ (“his wife”) as the object. Later in the verse, בְּנוֹ (“his son”) identifies Enoch as Cain’s son.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Abel’s brother.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּדַע קַיִן אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ, קַיִן is the subject of וַיֵּדַע ‘knew’. אֶת marks אִשְׁתּוֹ ‘his wife’ as the direct object. The possessive suffix makes אִשְׁתּוֹ definite.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected direct-object particle without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֵּדַע קַיִן אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ, the suffix refers to Cain. His wife is the object of וַיֵּדַע and the subject of וַתַּהַר וַתֵּלֶד, “she conceived and gave birth.”
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular construct noun with the third-person masculine singular possessive suffix ־וֹ.

analysis.evidence: The feminine singular subject is Cain’s wife. וַתַּהַר follows the statement that Cain knew his wife and precedes וַתֵּלֶד אֶת־חֲנוֹךְ, “and she bore Enoch,” placing conception between intercourse and birth.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ and an apocopated stem.

analysis.evidence: Cain’s wife is the subject of both וַתַּהַר (“she conceived”) and וַתֵּלֶד. The direct-object marker אֶת introduces חֲנוֹךְ (Enoch), the child she bore.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ.

analysis.evidence: In וַתֵּלֶד אֶת חֲנוֹךְ, “she bore Enoch,” אֶת marks the proper name חֲנוֹךְ as the definite direct object of וַתֵּלֶד.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַתֵּלֶד אֶת חֲנוֹךְ, אֶת marks Enoch as the child Cain’s wife bore. Later in the verse, כְּשֵׁם בְּנוֹ חֲנוֹךְ identifies Enoch as the son after whom Cain named the city.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי בֹּנֶה עִיר, וַיְהִי supplies the past tense for the masculine singular participle בֹּנֶה. Together they describe Cain’s ongoing activity, “and he was building a city.”
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ־ introduces a third-person masculine singular Qal wayyiqtol. There is no suffix.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: In וַיְהִי בֹּנֶה עִיר, the noun עִיר (“a city”) is the direct object of בֹּנֶה. With וַיְהִי, the participle describes Cain’s ongoing action (“he was building a city”).
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, agreeing with Cain.

draft.change: Add Genesis 11:5 to the verse evidence for the existing city sense of עִיר in article 3yr.
draft.definition: A built settlement, a city or town.
draft.evidence: Genesis 11:5 calls the settlement הָעִיר, “the city,” as it takes up the builders’ proposal for עִיר וּמִגְדָּל, “a city and a tower,” in Genesis 11:4.

analysis.evidence: In בֹּנֶה עִיר, “building a city,” עִיר is the direct object of בֹּנֶה. The next clause calls the same settlement הָעִיר, “the city,” and says Cain named it after his son Enoch.
analysis.morphology: Feminine singular absolute common noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם הָעִיר means “the name of the city.” The phrase כְּשֵׁם בְּנוֹ חֲנוֹךְ shows that Cain named the city after his son Enoch.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־.

draft.change: Add Genesis 10:25 as evidence for the existing identifying-name sense of שֵׁם at word index 0.
draft.definition: A name by which a person or other bearer is identified.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 10:25, אָחִיו identifies whose name is meant and יָקְטָן supplies that name.

analysis.evidence: שֵׁם הָעִיר means “the name of the city.” The following phrase כְּשֵׁם בְּנוֹ חֲנוֹךְ explains that Cain named the city after his son Enoch.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state before הָעִיר, with no prefix or suffix.

draft.change: Add Genesis 4:17 to the identifying-name sense of שֵׁם to document naming a place after a person.
draft.definition: The name by which someone is known, which can also be given to a place named after that person.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:17 identifies the son as Enoch and says that Cain called the city כְּשֵׁם בְּנוֹ, after his son’s name.

analysis.evidence: In כְּשֵׁם בְּנוֹ חֲנוֹךְ, the marked שֵׁם is the name of Cain’s son, Enoch. The prefix כְּ links it to שֵׁם הָעִיר earlier in the clause. Cain gives the city the same name his son bears.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed comparative preposition כְּ followed by a masculine singular construct noun, with בְּנוֹ as its complement.
analysis.sense: name by which someone is known

analysis.evidence: In כְּשֵׁם בְּנוֹ חֲנוֹךְ, “after the name of his son Enoch,” חֲנוֹךְ identifies Cain’s son, whose birth is recounted earlier in the verse. The city takes its name from him.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in apposition to בְּנוֹ, with no prefix or suffix.
